subtitle: A woman's question that weighed more than kings' treasure

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle portrait framed by shadowed halls of a Vedic household
panels.action: Maitreyi stands in a quiet courtyard of an ancient Videha home, one hand open toward a chest of ornaments set aside, her gaze lifted beyond the tiled roofs to a pale, endless sky.

dialogue.text: In the age of early Upanishads, when kings hoarded cattle and seers hoarded verses, Maitreyi asked a question so sharp it cut through wealth itself.

i18n.hi: उपनिषदों की भोर में, जब राजा गायें जोड़ते थे और ऋषि मंत्र, मैत्रेयी ने ऐसा सवाल किया जो सीधे दौलत को चीर गया

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Videha countryside with a modest but well-kept household in the mid-ground
panels.action: The camera floats above fields and groves near the kingdom of Videha, descending toward a large, orderly Vedic household where smoke curls from the altar and cattle graze beyond its fences.

dialogue.text: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad remembers a house in Videha, a world of fires, chants and herds, where a quiet decision would set a new kind of wealth before the world.

i18n.hi: बृहदारण्यक उपनिषद विदेह के एक घर को याद रखता है—अग्नि, मंत्र और पशुओं की दुनिया, जहाँ एक शांत फ़ैसले ने नई तरह की समृद्धि जग के सामने रख दी

panels.shot: medium shot inside a dim wooden hall with firelight flickering, focusing on ritual objects neatly arranged
panels.action: Within a timbered hall, ritual ladles, blackened pots and polished wooden spoons lie in careful rows beside stacks of grain and strings of ornaments hanging from a beam.

dialogue.text: Here, the old Vedic life revolved around sacrifice and order. Wealth meant cattle, grain, precious metal, and the right to pour offerings into the fire for men and gods.

i18n.hi: यहाँ पुरानी वैदिक ज़िंदगी यज्ञ और नियम के इर्द-गिर्द घूमती थी। धन मतलब गायें, अन्न, सोना–चाँदी, और देव–पुरुषों के लिए अग्नि में अर्पण का अधिकार

panels.shot: slow push-in on Maitreyi seated by the fire, profile visible, eyes intent on a recited verse
panels.action: Maitreyi sits cross-legged by the house-fire, a simple cloth over her shoulder, listening with a steady, burning gaze as unseen voices recite a solemn chant in the background.

dialogue.text: Tradition calls her a brahmavadini, a woman devoted to Brahman, the sacred word and the deep ground of things. Her name survives where almost every other female voice is lost.

i18n.hi: परंपरा उसे ब्रह्मवादिनी कहती है—ब्रह्म, वाणी और सत्य की साधिका। उसका नाम बचा रहा, जब लगभग हर औरत की आवाज़ मिट गई

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Maitreyi’s face lit by firelight, brows slightly furrowed in thought
panels.action: Firelight ripples across Maitreyi’s face, her brows drawn in quiet question as she watches a ladle rise and fall, thick smoke curling up toward the rafters.

dialogue.text: Yet even here, in the heart of ritual, a doubt grew. Could rites and cattle carry a person beyond decay, or was there some other path hidden beneath the chants?

i18n.hi: फिर भी, यहीं, अनुष्ठान के बीच, एक संदेह उगा। क्या यज्ञ और गायें इंसान को नाश से पार ले जा सकती हैं, या मन्त्रों के नीचे कोई और राह छिपी है?

panels.shot: imagined wide shot of a learned Brahmin figure preparing to depart, seen from behind Maitreyi’s shoulder
panels.action: From behind Maitreyi’s shoulder, we glimpse the strong outline of a departing householder, his hair tied, staff and bundle ready, as he surveys his orderly home one last time.

dialogue.text: The text speaks of Yajnavalkya, the learned householder, preparing to leave for the life of renunciation, to go from fires and family into the forest of thought.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ याज्ञवल्क्य का ज़िक्र करता है—विद्वान गृहस्थ, जो सन्यास के लिए तैयार है, अग्नि और परिवार से उठकर विचार के वन में जाने को

panels.shot: medium shot of Maitreyi turning toward the imagined figure, her body angled, curiosity and concern in her eyes
panels.action: Maitreyi turns sharply toward the man by the doorway, her posture straight, eyes clear and questioning as light from outside frames his silhouette.

dialogue.speaker: maitreyi
dialogue.text: If you are leaving, what will you leave behind for us?

i18n.hi: अगर आप जा रहे हैं, तो हमारे लिए क्या छोड़ेंगे?

panels.shot: low-angle medium showing chests of goods, cattle visible through the doorway, Maitreyi standing between them and the departing figure
panels.action: Large wooden chests sit open, ornaments and cloth folded within, while beyond the doorway cattle drift in the yard; Maitreyi stands between house and world, calm but tense.

dialogue.text: The tradition remembers his offer in plain words: he would divide his cattle, his property, his ornaments. It was the logical gift of a householder who leaves.

i18n.hi: परंपरा उसका सीधा प्रस्ताव दोहराती है: वह अपनी गायें, संपत्ति, गहने बाँटेगा। यही घर छोड़ते गृहस्थ की तर्कसंगत भेंट थी

panels.shot: tight medium shot of Maitreyi beside an open chest of ornaments, her hand hovering over them but not touching
panels.action: Beside an overflowing chest of gleaming ornaments, Maitreyi’s hand hovers in mid-air, fingers tense, as her gaze lifts away from the treasure toward something unseen.

dialogue.speaker: maitreyi
dialogue.text: If this whole earth filled with wealth were mine, would I become immortal by it?

i18n.hi: अगर यह सारी धरती धन से भरकर मेरी हो जाए, तो क्या मैं उससे अमर हो जाऊँगी?

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Maitreyi’s lips and jaw, the question hanging in the air, background softly blurred
panels.action: Her lips are slightly parted, jaw set, as if the question itself were a blade; behind her, jewels blur into vague shapes, their shine dim against her voice.

dialogue.text: These are among the oldest preserved words placed in a named Indian woman’s mouth. They do not ask for more ornaments. They ask whether wealth can buy freedom from death.

i18n.hi: ये उन सबसे प्राचीन पंक्तियों में हैं जो किसी नामदार भारतीय स्त्री के मुँह पर रखी गईं। वे और गहने नहीं माँगतीं, वे पूछती हैं: क्या दौलत मौत से मुक्ति खरीद सकती है?

panels.shot: medium shot with Maitreyi in foreground, the departing figure answering calmly in the background, both in profile
panels.action: In profile, Maitreyi stands firm in the foreground as the man behind her answers, his posture relaxed but solemn, one hand open in a small, conceding gesture.

dialogue.text: The answer is simple and devastating: "No." Wealth, even as wide as the earth, cannot buy immortality. It can only make life comfortable, and then it ends.

i18n.hi: जवाब सीधा और चुभता है: "नहीं।" धन, चाहे धरती जितना हो, अमरता नहीं खरीद सकता। बस जीवन थोड़ी देर सुखी करता है, फिर ख़त्म

panels.shot: close-up on Maitreyi’s eyes, reflecting the glint of ornaments below and the shadow of the departing figure above
panels.action: Maitreyi’s eyes catch twin reflections: the flicker of gold in the chest at her feet and the dark outline of the man turning away toward the forest path.

dialogue.speaker: maitreyi
dialogue.text: What shall I do with that which will not make me immortal?

i18n.hi: जिससे अमरता नहीं मिले, उसका मैं क्या करूँ?

panels.shot: wide shot of the hall as Maitreyi steps away from the chests, choosing instead to sit near the hearth facing the teacher
panels.action: Pulling back, we see Maitreyi step away from the open chests and sit once more near the hearth, facing the man now seated opposite her, their gazes level and unblinking.

dialogue.text: In that turning of her body away from the chests, the Upanishad stages its own turn: from ritual payment to inner seeking, from cattle to a different kind of gain.

i18n.hi: उसका संदूक से देह मोड़ना ही उपनिषद का मोड़ है—यज्ञ–दक्षिणा से भीतर की खोज की ओर, गायों से एक और तरह के लाभ की ओर

panels.shot: slow push-in on both figures seated face to face, the space between them charged, background darkened
panels.action: Against a darkened background, Maitreyi and her teacher sit facing each other, the small space between them lit by a single steady flame, as if the whole house has fallen silent.

dialogue.text: She asks for instruction instead of property. The scene is stripped bare: no altar, no king, no crowd, only a woman and a teacher and a question about what does not die.

i18n.hi: वह संपत्ति के बदले शिक्षा माँगती है। दृश्य खाली है—न वेदी, न राजा, न भीड़; बस एक स्त्री, एक शिक्षक, और यह सवाल कि क्या नाश के पार जाता है

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot where the household fades into a hint of forest and open sky beyond the walls
panels.action: The walls of the house seem to thin; beyond them we glimpse forest trees and open sky, as if the conversation has already stepped beyond the household into a wider, unseen space.

dialogue.text: From here the text moves into one of its boldest teachings: that the self, Atman, is not secured by possessions, but known by turning inward, by seeing that every love is for the sake of this self.

i18n.hi: यहीं से पाठ अपनी साहसी शिक्षा पर उतरता है: आत्मा, आत्मन, चीज़ों से नहीं बचती, भीतर मुड़ने से जानी जाती है—यह देखकर कि हर प्रेम अंततः इसी आत्म के लिए है

panels.shot: close-up on Maitreyi listening intently, her head slightly tilted, lips parted, absorbing the teaching
panels.action: Maitreyi leans in, her head slightly tilted, lips parted in silent amazement, as unseen words seem to pour toward her, the firelight now steady and gentle on her features.

dialogue.text: In some versions she protests when told the teaching may confuse her. The dialogue itself preserves the tension between guarding doctrine and letting a sharp mind follow it to the end.

i18n.hi: कुछ रूपों में वह आपत्ति करती है, जब उसे कहा जाता है कि यह ज्ञान उसे उलझा देगा। खुद संवाद में तनाव दर्ज है—शास्त्र की रक्षा और तेज दिमाग को अंत तक जाने देने के बीच

panels.shot: medium shot of Maitreyi framed by the textual image of a palm-leaf manuscript appearing faintly behind her
panels.action: Behind Maitreyi’s calm seated form, faint outlines of palm-leaf manuscripts hover, script lines running like quiet rivers, as if her question has been pressed into leaf and memory.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, the same dialogue appears twice in the Brihadaranyaka, in slightly different forms. Scholars see layers of composition, but the core remains: her refusal of wealth, her hunger for what lasts.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, यही बातचीत बृहदारण्यक में दो बार आती है, थोड़ा बदलते रूप में। विद्वान उसमें परतें देखते हैं, पर केंद्र वही रहता है: उसका धन से इनकार, उसकी प्यास उस चीज़ के लिए जो टिकती है

panels.shot: wide shot spanning centuries: Maitreyi in foreground, distant silhouettes of later commentators like faint shadows behind
panels.action: Maitreyi sits in clear focus, while behind her, like faint shadows on a wall, stand indistinct figures of later commentators, scrolls in hand, their outlines merging into the darkness.

dialogue.text: Medieval thinkers like Sureshvara would argue over these very lines, treating her question and his answer as serious philosophy, not household chatter, building whole systems on this small scene.

i18n.hi: सूरेश्वर जैसे मध्यकालीन दार्शनिक इन्हीं पंक्तियों पर बहस करेंगे—उसके सवाल और उसके उत्तर को गंभीर दर्शन मानकर, न कि घर की गप, और पूरे विचार–तंत्र इस छोटे से दृश्य पर खड़े करेंगे

panels.shot: close-up on a modern scholar’s hand turning a printed page where Maitreyi’s name is visible, dissolving back into Maitreyi’s steady face
panels.action: A modern hand turns a printed page where the name ‘Maitreyi’ stands in black letters, and as the page turns, it dissolves into Maitreyi’s face again, unchanged and quietly resolute.

dialogue.text: Historians warn us: we cannot recover her full life. Yet across two and a half millennia, these few attributed words let a woman stand at the root of a question India still asks.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार सावधान करते हैं: उसका पूरा जीवन हम नहीं पा सकते। पर ढाई हज़ार साल पार, ये थोड़े से शब्द एक स्त्री को उस मूल सवाल की जड़ में खड़ा कर देते हैं जिसे भारत आज भी पूछता है

panels.shot: final slow pull-back from Maitreyi seated peacefully in the empty hall, chests of wealth closed and pushed aside, sky visible through the doorway
panels.action: In the quiet hall, the chests of wealth now stand closed and pushed into shadow, while Maitreyi sits at ease near the doorway, framed by open sky and the faint outline of distant fields.

dialogue.text: Her refusal of the world’s wealth was not a gesture of disdain, but a demand that any true teaching face the one bargain no coin can buy—and that is why her question still weighs on us today.

i18n.hi: दुनिया की दौलत ठुकराना उसका घृणा का इशारा नहीं, यह माँग थी कि हर सच्ची शिक्षा उस सौदे का सामना करे जिसे कोई सिक्का नहीं खरीद सकता—और यही वजह है कि उसका सवाल आज भी हमें तौलता रहता है

title_i18n.en: Maitreyi Refuses the Wealth of the World
title_i18n.hi: मैत्रेयी ने दुनिया की दौलत ठुकरा दी

subtitle_i18n.en: A woman's question that weighed more than kings' treasure
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक औरत का सवाल, राजाओं के ख़ज़ाने से भारी
